Published online:
    September 4, 2026

Geographic focus:
    United States

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    Investors are focused on the upcoming August CPI print (Sept 11) as the key determinant of whether the Fed hikes at its Sept 15-16 meeting. Markets are roughly 50/50 on a hike. Fed Governor Waller signaled comfort holding rates steady if inflation continues cooling, pulling rate hike odds lower. Goldman Sachs baseline is a hold, with a hike conditional on hot CPI/PPI. S&P 500 is near all-time highs (+13% YTD) but faces seasonal headwinds in September, elevated yields near 4.77%, and uncertainty around AI sector momentum post the July unwind.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES — directly covers Fed rate trajectory, Treasury yields (10Y at 4.77%), CPI/PPI data, equity valuations, and S&P 500 pricing dynamics.

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 75 — a rate hike at the Sept meeting is a live, material scenario discussed throughout.
Probability of increase: ~50% (Fed funds futures imply roughly even odds at time of writing, conditional on CPI/PPI outcome)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 70 — Waller's comments and Goldman's base case anchor the hold scenario as the slight lean.
Probability of holding: ~50% (mirror of hike odds; Goldman baseline, contingent on benign inflation data)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 5 — cuts are not discussed; the debate is strictly hike vs. hold.
Probability of decrease: ~0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: -20 (Marginally dovish lean at the margin — Waller's late-Thursday comments tilted odds away from a hike and Goldman moved to a hold base case, but a hike remains very much live, keeping overall tone cautious rather than clearly dovish)
